text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Four Santa Claus held a symbolic picket near the Christmas tree beside the government building to protest against poverty.
- The government has agreed to postpone the introduction of compulsory motor insurance from January 1 to May 1 next year.
- The government will give interest-free loans to municipalities for paying wages to kindergarten teachers.
- National Radio and TV decides that beginning new year all films including episodes of sex and violence as well as drug abuse should be given special marking in TV programme guides.
- Estonian Tallinna Pank is to buy 20 percent of shares from Latvian Saules Banka worth 900.000 lats. The deal was approved last Friday at the meeting of Saules Banka's shareholders.

- December 20 was the last the last day for submitting applications to privatisations of the Latvian shipping company. Until the date the Latvian Privatisation Agency filed nine applications, including those of Nomura International plus Hansa Investments, Norwegian Finance group Morsoft and EBRD.
